details:
Loving imposters, however, I think we need a more clear indication that people are seeing an imposter. I get a lot of people now (in fact, most ._.) don’t know they are seeing my imposter or custom fallback, and just assume the no emissions, no gestures, and looking cruncher is just part of the avi, assuming just because they aren’t seeing a default generic public fallback, that it it’s just a normal avatar (happens a TON with imposters, but this problem has been around for agers with people that upload their own custom fallbacks).

Even if you’re friends, quest doesn’t un-imposter you until they fully show your avatar. I’ve had full hour long convos with people until they realised they weren’t seeing my avi and were seeing my imporster/fallback. You can't even tell if someone is seeing your fallback or not.

Firstly, perhaps a little icon on other user's nameplates to that are seeing your imposter/fallback would be good; just like the earmuff mode/player mute indicators.

And secondly, perhaps the little fallback icon is too small and overlooked since people see it so much and are used to it, or don't even have nameplates on. Perhaps a more obvious thing would be good (appearing now and then, so it isn’t there all the all the time), such as; a hula-hoop around the waist of the avi, either with text on it saying “imposter” or “fallback”, or just a simple coloured hoop indicator; or even a little sign next to or on the front, telling people it’s a fallback/imposter would be good!
title: Better fallback indication for custom fallbacks and imposters.
